title: Check if an image really is a PNG

seo.metaTitle: Verify If Image Is a PNG - Signature Check, Free
seo.metaDescription: Check whether pasted Base64 or data-URI content is really a PNG by looking at its file signature. Free, no upload - the text is checked in your browser.
seo.longDescription: A file extension is not proof: a JPG renamed to .png still has JPG bytes inside, and some downloads arrive with a name that does not match the content. This checker takes Base64 or a data URI, decodes it in your browser and looks at the signature at the start of the data. PNG always begins with the same eight bytes; anything else reports as not a PNG. The text never leaves your browser tab, which matters here more than usual, because pasted Base64 is often a secret - an API key, a session cookie or a signed URL.
howTo: Copy the Base64 string or the full data URI that you want to check.
Paste it into the text area - a data: prefix is stripped automatically.
Run the check and read the verdict.
A no means the content is a different format, or not an image at all.

faq.q: How does it decide that the content is a PNG?
faq.a: It decodes the Base64 in your browser and compares the first bytes against the PNG signature. A real PNG always starts with the same eight-byte marker; a renamed JPG does not.

faq.q: Can I paste a whole data URI?
faq.a: Yes. The data: prefix and the media type are stripped before decoding, so a complete src attribute value works as well as the Base64 part alone.

faq.q: Is my pasted string uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No, and this is the important part: the decoding and the check happen entirely in your browser tab. Pasted Base64 is often a credential or a signed link, so it is never sent to a server.

faq.q: It says no, but the file really is a PNG. Why?
faq.a: Usually the content is not valid Base64, was copied with line breaks and stray characters, or is a URL rather than the image data. Check that the text contains only Base64 characters.
